{{Technical|date=December 2019}}
In mathematics, the '''Jacobson&ndash;Morozov theorem''' is the assertion that [[nilpotent]] elements in a semi-simple [[Lie algebra]] can be extended to [[sl2-triple|sl<sub>2</sub>-triples]]. The theorem is named after {{harvnb|Jacobson|1951}}, {{harvnb|Morozov|1942}}.

==Statement==

The statement of Jacobson&ndash;Morozov relies on the following preliminary notions: an sl<sub>2</sub>-triple in a [[semi-simple Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak g</math> (throughout in this article, over a field of [[characteristic zero]]) is a [[homomorphism]] of Lie algebras <math>\mathfrak{sl}_2 \to \mathfrak g</math>. Equivalently, it is a triple <math>e, f, h</math> of elements in <math>\mathfrak g</math> satisfying the relations 
:<math>[h,e] = 2e, \quad [h,f] = -2f, \quad [e,f] = h. </math>
An element <math>x \in \mathfrak g</math> is called nilpotent, if the [[endomorphism]] <math>[x, -] : \mathfrak g \to \mathfrak g</math> (known as the [[adjoint representation]]) is a [[nilpotent endomorphism]]. It is an elementary fact that for any sl<sub>2</sub>-triple <math>(e, f, h)</math>, ''e'' must be nilpotent. The Jacobson&ndash;Morozov theorem states that, conversely, any nilpotent non-zero element <math>e \in \mathfrak g</math> can be extended to an sl<sub>2</sub>-triple.<ref>{{harvtxt|Bourbaki|2007|loc=Ch. VIII, §11, Prop. 2}}</ref><ref>{{harvtxt|Jacobson|1979|loc=Ch. III, §11, Theorem 17}}</ref> For <math>\mathfrak g = \mathfrak{sl}_n</math>, the sl<sub>2</sub>-triples obtained in this way are made explicit in {{harvtxt|Chriss|Ginzburg|1997|loc=p. 184}}.

The theorem can also be stated for [[linear algebraic group]]s (again over a field ''k'' of characteristic zero): any morphism (of algebraic groups) from the [[additive group]] <math>G_a</math> to a [[reductive group]] ''H'' factors through the embedding 
:<math>G_a \to SL_2, x \mapsto \left ( \begin{array}{cc} 1 & x \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \right ).</math>
Furthermore, any two such factorizations
:<math>SL_2 \to H</math>
are conjugate by a ''k''-point of ''H''.

==Generalization==
A far-reaching generalization of the theorem as formulated above can be stated as follows: the inclusion of pro-reductive groups into all linear algebraic groups, where morphisms <math>G \to H</math> in both categories are taken up to conjugation by elements in <math>H(k)</math>, admits a [[left adjoint]], the so-called pro-reductive envelope. This left adjoint sends the additive group <math>G_a</math> to <math>SL_2</math> (which happens to be semi-simple, as opposed to pro-reductive), thereby recovering the above form of Jacobson&ndash;Morozov.
This generalized Jacobson&ndash;Morozov theorem was proven by {{harvtxt|André|Kahn|2002|loc=Theorem 19.3.1}} by appealing to methods related to [[Tannakian category|Tannakian categories]] and by {{harvtxt|O'Sullivan|2010}} by more geometric methods.
